properties.statement: `add_verification` CANNOT SET `kind`, `status` OR `last_run_at`, SO RECORDING ONE VALIDATION TAKES FOUR CALLS AND THE NODE IS BORN AS THE VERY THING THE GAP SAID WAS INSUFFICIENT. Three reporters, dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08. (1) w-ec25cf2c, answering an `unvalidated_capability` gap for ONE capability, had to run: add_verification -> set_verification_kind(validation) -> verifies(...) -> set_verification_status(passing, last_run_at). `add_verification` accepts `method` and `level` but NOT `kind`, so a node created specifically to satisfy an unvalidated_capability gap is born `kind: verification` — which is exactly what that gap says is already present and not enough. THE DEFAULT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE INTENT IN THE ONE WORKFLOW THAT MOST OFTEN CREATES THESE. (2) w-fb7d30ab hit the other missing parameter: `add_verification` upserts name/level/method but has no `last_run_at`, so a node UPDATED to describe a NEW run keeps the OLD run's date. They re-ran stack_currency.py on 2026-08-07 and recorded the result into `ver:fleet_stack_currency_gate`; the node's text then described the 08-07 run while `last_run_at` still read `2026-08-03`. The node was internally inconsistent AND THE WRITE REPORTED SUCCESS with nothing saying so. They looked for a route out and could not find one — `reconcile_verification` looked like the intended path but takes real test-run outcomes, which is a different act from 're-ran a measurement script'. (3) 2026-08-08, w-4d05e937 (LANE UNSUSPECTED-VALIDATION-WALK) ADDS THE THIRD MISSING PARAMETER AND THE REASON IT IS WORSE THAN INCONVENIENT. `status` is missing too, so the node is born `kind: verification, status: planned` — THE EXACT TWO VALUES THAT MAKE IT NOT ANSWER THE GAP. Their framing is the one to keep: BETWEEN CALL 1 AND CALL 4 THE GRAPH HOLDS A NODE ASSERTING SOMETHING NOBODY MEANT, and on a `--shared` graph THAT WINDOW IS VISIBLE TO EVERY OTHER ATTACHED SESSION. What was a four-call annoyance on a single-writer store is a publication of a false claim on a shared one, for as long as the sequence takes. They filed it knowing the `kind` half was already reported, per the file's own no-dedup rule. FIX SHAPE, from all three: accept `kind`, `status`, `last_run_at` and a `verifies` target on add_verification, collapsing four calls to one; or have the gap's own prompt name the exact call sequence; and either accept `last_run_at` or have the upsert WARN when name/description change while last_run_at does not. THE REUSABLE FRAMING: a date that silently belongs to a previous run is the same failure class as 'a documented constant is not a measurement' — and an intermediate state visible to other writers is the same failure class as a non-atomic write.
properties.value: {"reported":"2026-08-07 w-ec25cf2c (kind) and w-fb7d30ab (last_run_at); 2026-08-08 w-4d05e937 (status + the shared-window consequence)","defect_a":"no kind param, so a node answering an unvalidated_capability gap is born kind: verification","defect_b":"no last_run_at param, so an updated node keeps the previous run's date and the write still reports success","defect_c":"no status param, so the node is born planned - with kind, the exact two values that fail to answer the gap","cost":"four calls to record one validation","shared_graph_consequence":"between call 1 and call 4 the graph publishes a claim nobody meant, visible to every attached session","no_workaround_found":"reconcile_verification takes test-run outcomes, a different act from re-running a measurement script","fix_shape":"accept kind, status, last_run_at and a verifies target on add_verification; warn when the description moves and last_run_at does not"}
